summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and opioid dependence was admitted after being found unresponsive with a high alcohol level. He was treated in the ICU for severe alcohol withdrawal using a phenobarbital taper and managed for complications including acute on chronic anemia, hepatic encephalopathy, and MRSA urinary tract infection. He developed bilateral lower extremity edema and erythema with concern for cellulitis and possible vascular compromise in the right great toe, which improved with antibiotics and diuresis. His liver function tests remained elevated, consistent with alcoholic hepatitis. He was stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, diuretics, lactulose, and methadone 70mg daily, with strict instructions to abstain from alcohol and follow up with liver and primary care specialists.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
